newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico business leaders cautious despite GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico business leaders cautious despite GDP data.

text.p: Although Mexican financial markets surged after the release of strong economic growth data on Wednesday, business leaders sounded a note of caution.

The encouraging figures, showing 5.1 percent growth in gross domestic product last year, confirmed the economy was on the mend, but the recovery had yet to find its way into people's pockets, they said.

"Beware. You all know there are lies, damned lies and then there are statistics. In this case averages flatter to deceive a little," said Carlos Abascal, president of the Mexican Employers' Confederation (Coparmex).
Financial professionals surveyed by Reuters in Mexico City had forecast on average a 4.65 percent year-on-year increase in GDP in 1996.

"It is good that GDP gained 5.1 percent, but private enterprise, the confederation, cannot but point out that huge challenges still lie ahead over employment, purchasing power and reviving the domestic market," Abascal told journalists.
The data did not signal an end to the economic crisis unleashed by a bungled devaluation of the Mexican peso in December 1994, he said.
"There is still no reason for us to hang out the flags and think we have triumphed over the problem we faced in December 1994," Abascal said.

In a separate interview with journalists, Hector Larios, president of the Business Coordinating Council (CCE), said the GDP data were encouraging but "this does not mean we have shrugged off the crisis."
